note: Tuvalu: Taiwanese enter without a visa for 90 days, nationals of the Schengen states, the EU but Ireland, and Serbia for 90 in 180; everyone else gets a visa on arrival for a month, free for the countries and territories listed and AUD 100 for the rest (the fee isn't modelled). Read from Wikipedia's copy. Checked on 2026-11-03 against the Immigration Regulations (CAP 24.15.1, 2022 revised edition), which give a visitors permit of at most 30 days, so Wikipedia's month was read as 30 days, free for Schedule 1's countries and $100 for the rest; the visa waivers (Taiwan, the Schengen states, the EU, Serbia) aren't in the Regulations and stand on Wikipedia's copy.

sources.title: Wikipedia, Visa policy of Tuvalu
sources.said: Citizens of the following countries and territories may enter Tuvalu without a visa for the following period: 90 days Taiwan 90 days within any 180 days European Union member states (except Ireland) Iceland Liechtenstein Norway Serbia Switzerland ... Citizens of the following countries and territories are not required to pay a visa fee. They may obtain a visa on arrival for a maximum stay of 1 month: American Samoa Antigua and Barbuda Bahamas Belize Cayman Islands Cook Islands Fiji Gambia Gibraltar Grenada Hong Kong Jamaica Kenya Kiribati Lesotho Malawi Malaysia Maldives Mauritius Montserrat Nauru Niue Northern Mariana Islands Samoa Saint Kitts and Nevis Saint Lucia Saint Vincent and the Grenadines South Korea Tanzania Tonga Trinidad and Tobago Uganda United Kingdom Vanuatu Zambia ... Citizens of other countries must obtain a visa on arrival for a maximum stay of 1 month. They must pay a visa fee ( AUD 100).

sources.title: Tuvalu, Immigration Regulations, CAP 24.15.1 (2022 Revised Edition), regulation 2 and Schedule 1 (Office of the Attorney-General's legislation site)
sources.said: 2 Visitors Permit (1) The Principal Immigration Officer may issue to any visitor a visitors permit for a maximum stay of 30 days under section 9 of the Act ... (a) a visitor who is a citizen of a country listed in Schedule 1 shall not pay a fee; (b) a visitor who is a citizen of a country not listed in Schedule 1 shall pay a fee of $100, unless the payment of such a fee is waived by the Minister. ...
